title: Could Iran cut the Gulf's internet cables?
credits: Photos: Anders Marlowe, Karthik B K, Chris LeBoutillier / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Iran is reportedly preparing a new kind of threat: cutting the internet under the sea.
Two senior Iranian security officials told Reuters that Tehran has detailed plans to target undersea communication cables in the Gulf.
They said the plans would be used if the United States and Israel attack Iran again.
One official said Iran would also try to block repairs, to make internet outages last longer.
Earlier, a Revolutionary Guards official, Yadollah Javani, said Iran could target seven major internet cables beneath the Strait of Hormuz.
Undersea cables carry about ninety-nine percent of global internet traffic, according to the UN's telecommunication agency.
But an expert at TeleGeography says less than one percent of international bandwidth passes through the Strait of Hormuz, so the global impact could be limited.
The Red Sea matters more. It carries around ten percent of internet traffic between regions.
According to Reuters, Iranian strikes hit two Amazon Web Services facilities in the UAE in March.
Analysts say the threats are meant to deter a new war, and to pressure Washington through worried Gulf governments.
The US State Department and Iran's foreign ministry did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment.
